risks.name: The computer's disk fills up
risks.risk: Docker's disk (both databases), the saved answers and the logs all live on this computer's drive, and they only grow.
risks.watch: How full the drive that holds OneTouch's folder and Docker's disk is.
risks.effect: Postgres can't save anything: sign-ins, assignments and notifications fail, and the databases may not start again.
risks.action: Free space on the drive (docker system prune, old downloads), or move Docker's disk to a bigger one.

risks.name: Postgres runs out of connections
risks.risk: The Node server, Cube and Metabase each keep connections open to the one Postgres server, and a stuck query holds one.
risks.watch: Connections in use, against Postgres's max_connections.
risks.effect: New connections are refused: sign-in, ticket data and dashboards fail for everyone at once.
risks.action: See what holds them (pg_stat_activity) and restart it, or raise max_connections.

risks.name: AI spending passes its daily budget
risks.risk: Every new question costs a little. A busy day, a big warm-up run or something asking in a loop adds up quickly.
risks.watch: What Claude cost in the last 24 hours (claude_usage), against a budget of $5 a day (CLAUDE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD).
risks.effect: More is being spent than planned. If the Anthropic workspace's spend limit is reached, new questions stop being answered.
risks.action: npm run usage shows who and what is asking. Raise the budget here, or the spend limit in Anthropic's console.

risks.name: Brevo's daily sending limit is reached
risks.risk: Brevo sends only so many emails a day on this plan. Email everyone on demo day, or a family of hundreds handed out, uses it fast.
risks.watch: Emails sent in the last 24 hours, against 300 a day (BREVO_DAILY_LIMIT).
risks.effect: Brevo refuses the rest of the day's emails. The 🔔 in the header still works.
risks.action: Switch Email everyone off, or move to a Brevo plan that sends more and raise BREVO_DAILY_LIMIT.

risks.name: The Node server runs out of memory
risks.risk: The ticket index, KPIs, chart results and saved answers are kept in memory. More tickets, or something that never lets go, makes them grow.
risks.watch: How much of its memory limit the Node server is using.
risks.effect: The server stops and restarts: everyone loses what they were doing, and the site is down for a few seconds.
risks.action: Restart the app, and look for what grew. If the data really grew, give Node more memory (--max-old-space-size).

risks.name: Someone is guessing passwords
risks.risk: Five wrong passwords lock an account for 15 minutes. One locked account is someone who forgot; several at once looks like guessing.
risks.watch: How many accounts are locked right now.
risks.effect: Those people can't sign in for 15 minutes, and someone may be trying to get in.
risks.action: See whose (npm run users -- list), and check who is reaching the site in Cloudflare.

example.name: Example: Cube runs out of memory
example.risk: For demos only. Cube keeps recent query results in memory; if it filled up, Cube would stop answering.
example.watch: A made-up reading. Once someone presses Run, it climbs from 52% to 100% in 4.5 seconds.
example.effect: If this were real: search, charts, KPIs and the AI assistant's answers would stop.
example.action: Nothing: it isn't real. Press Stop, or it ends by itself after 10 minutes.
